## Walkthrough

This pull request transforms a generic Chrome extension v3 starter into a functional "Journal-Gated URL Blocker" extension. The extension blocks navigation to URLs matching configured blocklist patterns, unless a matching keyword has been journaled recently. Changes span manifest configuration, a new popup interface for status display, a service worker that enforces blocking logic, utility functions for journal/settings parsing, and a settings page for configuration. The service worker intercepts `webNavigation.onCommitted` events, checks URLs against block patterns, fetches cached journal CSV data, and conditionally redirects blocked pages. The popup displays current URL status, while the settings page allows configuration of blocklist patterns, journal CSV URL, keywords, timeframe window, and redirect destination.

## Sequence Diagram

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant User as User/Browser
    participant SW as Service Worker
    participant Storage as chrome.storage.sync
    participant JournalServer as Journal Server
    participant Tab as Tab/Page

    User->>Tab: Navigate to URL
    Tab->>SW: onCommitted event (URL)
    
    SW->>Storage: Load extension settings
    Storage-->>SW: Return settings (blocklist, journalUrl, keywords, timeframe, blockUrl)
    
    SW->>SW: Parse blocklist patterns
    SW->>SW: Check if URL matches any pattern
    
    alt URL does not match blocklist
        SW->>Tab: Allow navigation (no action)
    else URL matches blocklist pattern
        SW->>JournalServer: Fetch journal CSV (cached)
        JournalServer-->>SW: Return CSV entries (timestamp, text)
        
        SW->>SW: Parse CSV entries
        SW->>SW: Extract keywords from settings
        SW->>SW: Compute recent timeframe cutoff
        SW->>SW: Check if any recent entry contains keywords
        
        alt Recent entry contains keyword
            SW->>Tab: Allow navigation (keyword matched)
        else No keyword match found
            SW->>Tab: Redirect to blockUrl
        end
    end
```

## Code Review

This pull request implements a 'Journal-Gated URL Blocker' extension that restricts access to websites based on recent journal entries. Key additions include a background service worker for navigation monitoring, a settings page for configuration, and a status popup. Review feedback highlights several critical improvements: optimizing storage access to avoid rate limits, preventing infinite redirect loops when the block URL matches the blocklist, reducing code duplication by sharing utilities, and using persistent storage for the journal cache to handle service worker termination in Manifest V3.

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

Accessing `chrome.storage.sync` on every navigation event is inefficient and can hit API rate limits, especially if the user has many tabs open or navigates frequently. It is recommended to load the settings into a local variable at startup and keep it updated using the `chrome.storage.onChanged` listener.

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

This logic can lead to an infinite redirect loop if the `blockUrl` itself matches a pattern in the `blocklist`. For example, if `example.com` is blocked and the redirect URL is `https://example.com/blocked`, the extension will repeatedly redirect to the block page. Adding a check to ensure the current URL is not the redirect target prevents this.

```suggestion
  if (url === s.blockUrl || !urlMatchesAnyPattern(url, blockPatterns)) return;
```

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

The `DEFAULT_SETTINGS` object and utility functions (`parseLines`, `urlMatchesAnyPattern`) are duplicated from `service-worker-utils.js`. This increases maintenance overhead and the risk of desynchronization. Since this is a Chrome extension, you can share the code by including the root utility file in `popup.html` using a `<script src="/service-worker-utils.js"></script>` tag before `popup.js`.

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

In Manifest V3, service workers are ephemeral and can be terminated by the browser after a short period of inactivity. When this happens, the in-memory `journalCache` variable is lost. To ensure the cache persists for the intended `CACHE_TTL_MS` regardless of worker suspension, consider using `chrome.storage.session` to store the cached data.

`Does the Chrome Extensions `chrome.webNavigation.onCommitted` event fire only after a navigation has committed, and can it prevent the target page from loading?`

💡 Result:

Yes: chrome.webNavigation.onCommitted fires when the browser “has decided to switch to the new document” (i.e., after the navigation is committed), though the document/resources may still be downloading. [1][2] No: onCommitted itself cannot be used to prevent the target page from loading. The event is informational (“Fired when a navigation is committed… the browser has decided to switch…”), and the Chrome Extensions webNavigation API doesn’t provide a way to cancel/stop in-flight navigations from an onCommitted listener. [1][2] If you need to stop/cancel navigation, you must do it earlier (e.g., onBeforeNavigate) or via other APIs that support blocking/redirecting before the page loads (for example, using blocking webRequest listeners rather than waiting for onCommitted). [2][3] Practical nuance: running logic on onCommitted may still happen “before resources are fully loaded” (before onDOMContentLoaded/onCompleted), but the navigation has already been committed and the browser has switched to the new document at that point. [1][2]

Citations:

- 1: https://developers.chrome.com/docs/extensions/reference/webNavigation
- 2: https://developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/reference/api/webNavigation
- 3: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/39333408/block-the-navigation-indicated-by-an-onbeforenavigate-event-in-a-chrome-extensio

**`onCommitted` is too late for a real blocker—use `onBeforeNavigate` instead.**

The `chrome.webNavigation.onCommitted` event fires after the browser has already committed to the navigation; at that point, the navigation is irreversible and the target page begins rendering. Redirecting with `chrome.tabs.update()` after commitment is too late—the page has already been switched to. To truly block navigation before the page loads, use `onBeforeNavigate` (which allows you to redirect before commit) or a blocking webRequest listener. The current approach violates the "access only if…" requirement because the blocked page's navigation is committed before the redirect logic even runs.

The `chrome.webNavigation.onCommitted` event fires after the browser has already committed to the navigation; at that point, the navigation is irreversible and the target page begins rendering.
